body.statement: For every finite \(J\), every \(L\ge1\), and each \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\), \(\mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H\subseteq\mathcal C_{H,L}+[-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m\). Consequently, for every probability table \(R\), \(\max\{0,d_{H,L}(R)-e_{H,L}\}\le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)\le d_{H,L}(R)\). For rational \(R\), the finite convex-hull program admits rational primal and dual certificates \(d^-\le d_{H,L}(R)\le d^+\) with any prescribed positive rational gap; in particular, \(L_n=n\) and \(\eta_n=1/n\) yield \(d^+-d^-\le\eta_n\) and \(\underline D_{H,n}=\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}\le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H)\). Refinement reaches any requested strictly positive distance precision.
body.justification: The moment vector has affine dimension at most \(m-1\), so every quadratic image point has an equal-moment representative on at most \(\min\{|H|,m\}\) tables and the grid error avoids exponential response-table dependence.
body.gap: Duarte et al. Theorem 1 on p. 7 proves sharpness of Algorithm 2's polynomial program, while Section 5 on pp. 8--10 and Algorithm 3 provide interruptible, progressively refined valid bounds and \(\varepsilon\)-sharpness. That general program does not give this conditional-iid quadratic-body grid sandwich, its closed deterministic error, or separate finite-stratum and terminal certificates; Kitamura--Stoye test a polyhedral random-utility cone.
body.consumer: Cells with more than three plans receive auditable included-point certificates, excluded-point separators, and a stopping rule at any positive tolerance.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(H\in\{F_\kappa,F_\infty\}\) and write \(N=|H|\).  First, \(H\) is nonempty.  For finite \(\kappa\), choose \(z\) outside the finite collection of tie hyperplanes and let its strict maximizers in all required contexts define \(f\); then all constraints of \(G_{\kappa,f}\) hold, so \(f\in F_\kappa\).  For the terminal set, choose an unbounded sequence \(\kappa_j\) and such an induced table at every \(\kappa_j\).  Since there are finitely many tables, one table \(f\) occurs along an unbounded subsequence.  Every affine cycle weight \(A_C+B_C\kappa_j\) for that table is positive on this subsequence.  Hence \(B_C>0\), or \(B_C=0\) and \(A_C>0\); \(B_C<0\) is impossible.  Thus \(f\in F_\infty\).

Take \(q\in\Delta(H)\).  By \(\texttt{lem:observable-moment-compression}\), there is \(\bar q\in\Delta(H)\) with
\[
 v(\bar q)=v(q),
 \qquad h:=|\operatorname{supp}(\bar q)|\le\min\{N,m\}.
\]
If \(h=1\), then \(\bar q\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\) for every \(L\), so set \(q'=\bar q\).  If \(h\ge2\), order its support as \(f_1,\ldots,f_h\) and define
\[
 q'_{f_j}=\frac{\lfloor L\bar q_{f_j}\rfloor}{L}\quad(j<h),
 \qquad
 q'_{f_h}=1-\sum_{j<h}q'_{f_j},
\]
with all other coordinates zero.  Then \(q'\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\), and
\[
 \|\bar q-q'\|_1
 =2\sum_{j<h}\left(\bar q_{f_j}-q'_{f_j}\right)
 \le\frac{2(h-1)}{L}
 \le\frac{2(\min\{N,m\}-1)}{L}.
\]
For any two probability vectors \(x,x'\) on \(H\) and any subset \(E\subseteq H\), cancellation of the total signed mass gives
\[
 |x(E)-x'(E)|\le\frac12\|x-x'\|_1.
\]
Both \(r_a\) and \(s_{ab}\) are probabilities of subsets of \(H\).  With \(\Delta=\|\bar q-q'\|_1\), therefore,
\[
 |r_a(\bar q)-r_a(q')|\le\frac\Delta2,
 \qquad
 |s_{ab}(\bar q)-s_{ab}(q')|\le\frac\Delta2.
\]
Because all factors lie in \([0,1]\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |v_{ab}(q)-v_{ab}(q')|
 &=|v_{ab}(\bar q)-v_{ab}(q')|\\
 &\le |r_a(\bar q)-r_a(q')|s_{ab}(\bar q)
      +r_a(q')|s_{ab}(\bar q)-s_{ab}(q')|\\
 &\le\Delta.
\end{aligned}
\]
The left side is also at most one.  With the corrected construction
\[
 e_{H,L}=\min\left\{1,\frac{2(\min\{N,m\}-1)}{L}\right\},
\]
we have proved \(\|v(q)-v(q')\|_\infty\le e_{H,L}\).

The grid image is contained in the full image, so \(\mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H\).  Conversely, for
\[
 Q=\sum_{j=1}^s\theta_jv(q^j)\in\mathcal C_H,
 \qquad \theta_j\ge0,
 \qquad \sum_j\theta_j=1,
\]
apply the preceding compression and rounding separately to each \(q^j\), producing \(q^{j\prime}\in\mathcal G_{H,L}\).  Then
\[
 Q_L=\sum_j\theta_jv(q^{j\prime})\in\mathcal C_{H,L},
 \qquad
 \|Q-Q_L\|_\infty
 \le\sum_j\theta_j\|v(q^j)-v(q^{j\prime})\|_\infty
 \le e_{H,L}.
\]
This proves
\[
 \mathcal C_{H,L}\subseteq\mathcal C_H
 \subseteq\mathcal C_{H,L}+[-e_{H,L},e_{H,L}]^m.
\]

Both bodies are compact.  The first inclusion gives
\[
 \operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)\le d_{H,L}(R).
\]
For a nearest \(Q\in\mathcal C_H\), take the preceding \(Q_L\).  The triangle inequality yields
\[
 d_{H,L}(R)
 \le\|R-Q_L\|_\infty
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(R,\mathcal C_H)+e_{H,L}.
\]
Rearranging and using nonnegativity proves the two-sided distance bound.

For rational certification, enumerate the finite grid image as rational vectors \(x^1,\ldots,x^G\).  For rational \(R\), \(d_{H,L}(R)\) is the value of the rational linear program
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{minimize}&\delta\\
 \text{over}&\delta\ge0,\ \omega_g\ge0\\
 \text{subject to}&\displaystyle\sum_{g=1}^G\omega_g=1,\\
 &\displaystyle-\delta\le R_j-\sum_{g=1}^G\omega_gx^g_j\le\delta,
 \quad j=1,\ldots,m.
\end{array}
\]
The corresponding lower-certificate system is
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
 \text{maximize}&u^\top R-t\\
 \text{over}&u=u^+-u^-,\quad u^+,u^-\ge0,\quad t\in\mathbb R\\
 \text{subject to}&\displaystyle\sum_{j=1}^m(u_j^++u_j^-)\le1,\\
 &t\ge u^\top x^g,\quad g=1,\ldots,G.
\end{array}
\]
Indeed, for every primal mixture \(x=\sum_g\omega_gx^g\) and every displayed lower certificate,
\[
 u^\top R-t\le u^\top(R-x)\le\|R-x\|_\infty,
\]
which is weak duality.  If the minimum is zero, \(u=0\) and \(t=0\) give equality.  If it is positive, then at a minimizing point \(x^*\), the active signed coordinates of \(R-x^*\) generate a supporting functional \(u\) of \(\ell_1\)-norm one for the minimizing face; otherwise a convex combination of grid points would give a feasible direction that strictly decreases every active signed residual, contradicting minimality.  For this \(u\), set \(t=\max_gu^\top x^g=u^\top x^*\).  Then
\[
 u^\top R-t=u^\top(R-x^*)=\|R-x^*\|_\infty=d_{H,L}(R),
\]
so the two certificate systems have the same value.  All constraints are rational.  Enumerating their finitely many active sets and solving each full-rank subsystem by rational Gaussian elimination yields rational optimal basic feasible certificates; direct substitution checks every inequality and equality.  Stopping earlier with feasible upper and lower certificates whose objective values differ by at most any prescribed positive rational tolerance gives rational \(d^-\le d_{H,L}(R)\le d^+\).

With \(L_n=n\), \(\eta_n=1/n\), and \(R=\widehat P\), rationality follows from the multinomial counts.  The certified inequalities and the deterministic sandwich give
\[
 \underline D_{H,n}
 =\max\{0,d^-_{H,n}-e_{H,L_n}\}
 \le\operatorname{dist}_\infty(\widehat P,\mathcal C_H).
\]
Finally \(e_{H,L}\to0\) for fixed finite \(H\), now at the observable-compressed rate \(2(\min\{|H|,m\}-1)/L\), and the primal--dual gap can be made arbitrarily small.  Choosing both errors below half of any requested positive tolerance proves finite refinement to that distance precision.
